**Decision.**
1. **The full-page capture is quantized, not only recompressed.** Lossless oxipng (`-o max --strip safe`) reached 946,308 bytes, and the capture is 1440 by 11,353 pixels of text. It has 695 colors. A palette of 256 colors without dithering is nearly exact (PSNR 69.9 dB) but weighs 456,489 bytes even with zopfli, so the palette had to shrink. pngquant's 64 colors without dithering, with zopfli, gave 392,364 bytes, and a crop at twice the size showed the project's orange status dot turned tan: pngquant weighs colors by area, and the saturated accents are small. So the palette kept is pngquant's 64 colors plus the 16 colors of the source it mapped worst, chosen one by one by pixel count times squared distance (the status dot, the link blue, the labels' orange and their edges), each source color mapped to its nearest entry, no dithering, then `oxipng -o max -Z --strip safe`. The result is 398,678 bytes, 80 colors, still 1440 by 11,353: PSNR 61.2 dB against the source, 0.01 % of the pixels off by more than 8 levels. The status dot, the link and the labels compared at twice the size show no difference.
2. **"Over 200 KB" is read as over 200,000 bytes.** The tracked PNGs over that, besides the capture, are four of `app/screenshots/` (`tower-light-1440`, `tower-dark-1440`, `tower-dark-768`, `tower-light-768`, 204,287 to 211,862 bytes), outside `docs/` but covered by the same promise. Lossless oxipng was enough for them: 155,421 to 161,519 bytes, each pixel the same, the dimensions unchanged. `--strip safe` dropped nothing: the files had no chunk beyond the image's own.
3. **The check is a test, not a guard rule.** `v2/test/docs-png-size.test.ts` lists the PNGs git tracks under `docs/` and fails on any over 500,000 bytes, naming each with its size. It runs in the `v2` workflow's `npm test`, on every pull request to `v2`. Reading every tracked file rather than a diff refuses a new capture and an existing one that grows alike, and needs no base. 500 KB is counted as 500,000 bytes, the stricter reading.
4. **Same paths.** Each file was replaced in place, so no Markdown link changed. `docs/v2/ui-overhaul/before/README.md` says the capture is 11,353 pixels tall, which stays true.

**Tests first.** `a649f7cf` committed the test alone; on it, the test failed with `docs/v2/ui-overhaul/before/proofmulti-inbox-full-page.png: 1179969 bytes`. It passes from the next commit, which compresses that capture.

**Not done here.**
- **No matrix line.** None names this promise, and a new `P` id could meet a parallel milestone 6 lane's; the orchestrator gives it one at the merge if the matrix should carry it.
- PNGs under 200,000 bytes were left as they are, and PNGs outside `docs/` are not checked by the test.
- The test runs in the `v2` workflow, on pull requests and pushes to `v2`. `checks.yml` runs only the root `test/`, so a pull request straight to `main` is not checked by it.

**Checks**, on this branch at `origin/v2` `0e49cbde`:
- `npm run typecheck` in `v2/`: clean.
- `npm test` in `v2/`: 2872 Node tests, 2737 pass, 135 skipped, 0 fail; 415 Vitest tests pass.
- `npm run guard -- --base origin/v2`: nothing refused. The guard does not read `docs/v2/`, so the lane's diff was also searched for the owner's name, the organisation's and the first piloted project's: none.

**Resources.** No Docker object, no port, no tunnel, no secret, no Claude Code login read. Network: `git fetch`, `npm ci` of the lock file, the Debian packages of pngquant 2.18.0 and libimagequant (`apt-get download`, unpacked without installing), oxipng 9.1.5's release archive from its GitHub repository, and Pillow and NumPy from PyPI into a scratch folder to compare the pixels; all of these outside the repository. GitHub for the pull request.

- Pull request: 457, against `v2`.
- Author: Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), lane `v2-j6-png-compress`.

## 2026-10-28: a setup check a restart interrupts is released at the next start, and the flow's git asks gh for GitHub's credential with no app (the author's choices, lane `v2-j6-setup-robustness`, C4, P258, B6.5, P262, issues #436 and #421)

**The need.** Two gaps the milestone 5 lanes left open. #436: a setup session's check (`checkBranch`, `checkPrepared`) removes what it made in a `finally`, which a stop of the service never runs, so its containers, network, images and tree stay, under a session id no ledger row knows. #421: on a Compose install with no GitHub App, the flow's fetches and pushes take git's environment from `lib/forge.ts`, which then names no helper that reads `GH_TOKEN`, so a private repository is refused. Tests first, French and English for any person's text (none was added: the new lines are the service's log, in English as the others), nothing on a real server, no deploy.

**The branch.** Renamed to `v2-j6-setup-robustness`, from `origin/v2` at `0e49cbde`.

**Decision.**
1. **#436: the check's folder is its record, released by its id.** The issue offered two ways: remove at start whatever carries `cleared.role=env-check`, or record the check's id so the restart recovery releases it. A sweep by role would also remove a running check of another instance on the same host, which `releaseStopped` was written never to do, so the second way was taken. The record already existed: `<state>/env-check/<session id>`, the folder of the branch's tree. It is now made first, before any Docker object, in both checks. At start, beside `recover()`, the runtime calls `releaseInterruptedChecks`: each folder named by a session id that no check of this process runs is released by that id (`removeSession`: containers, network, images), then removed. The checks this process runs are known in memory: the engine can be built after the assistant writes the workspace (issue #420), while the environment step already runs a check in the same process, which a sweep by folder alone would kill. A removal that fails is said by id and keeps its folder, at start and at a check's own end, so the next start tries again; before, the folder went whatever Docker said. Only this state folder is read, so another instance's checks are never named.
2. **#436: the ticket fails cleanly; it is not resumed.** The restart recovery already puts a ticket left In Progress back in Todo with the restart note, and the adapter keeps nothing to resume a session with, so an interrupted check's ticket goes back as any other. No round is recorded for a check that never answered, so its next start counts its rounds from one. The environment step keeps no state across a restart (its queue is in memory): a service whose check was interrupted shows its ready image with no check, and Build runs it again.
3. **#421: neither option of the issue as written.** (a), the helper in `lib/forge.ts`'s ambient environment, would change every v1 install's git and break the v1 test that pins the ambient credential "exactly as before" (`test/forge.test.ts`). (b), `gh auth setup-git` in the image's entrypoint, runs before the assistant gives the service its token: the forge step sets `GH_TOKEN` in the running service (`setup/steps/forge.ts`), and `gh auth setup-git` refuses with no credential (tried once with an empty `HOME` and no credential, it said it was not logged into any GitHub host and exited 1). So the helper is added where v2 reads `lib/forge.ts`'s environments, `forgeEnvironments`, the one door of `flow/effects.ts`, `flow/runtime.ts`, `modules/lead.ts` and `lead/briefing.ts`: its child now also says whether the forge is the ambient credential (`forgeMode`), and only then git's environment goes through `cloneEnvironment`, the function of the workspace step's clones. With a GitHub App, git keeps the forge's helper alone: an empty helper after it would have dropped the app's for the personal token. `cloneEnvironment` now also drops git's debug switches (`GIT_TRACE`, `GIT_TRACE_CURL`, `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE`, `GIT_TRACE_REDACT`, the git part of `lib/forge.ts`'s list) when it adds the helper: a failed git's last lines go into the service's log through `CheckoutError`.
4. **#421: the token's places, checked.** gh reads `GH_TOKEN` from its own environment; it is in no git setting, argument, URL or output. A session's container gets only the variables it is given by name, and the Docker client runs with the service's environment, so a bare `--env GH_TOKEN` would leak it: a test starts a session and a check with `GH_TOKEN` set and finds the name and the value in no container's arguments or private environment. Issue #147 (code a session runs reading the session's own token) is not this lane's and is unchanged.

**Tests first.**
- #436, `test/flow/env-setup.test.ts`: the real `checkBranch` on the fake `docker` with its check's `exec` never answering, so its `finally` never runs; then a new engine on the same ledger and the release at start. Before the code, the test file did not load (`releaseInterruptedChecks` missing). Two more cases: a check this process runs is left alone and a failed removal keeps its folder; the runtime, once it builds its engine, releases what a folder names. That last case failed with the runtime's call taken out.
- #421, `test/workspace/forge-git.test.ts`, over the real `lib/forge.ts` child and a fake gh on PATH: the ambient case failed with no helper (`actual: []`); the app case and the no-token case passed before and after, as they must. git's own `git credential fill` for a private repository on GitHub gets the value from gh, and its output does not hold it. `test/container/session-runtime.test.ts`: the session's and the check's containers, which passed before and after; it guards.

**The real run.** On this server, outside any container, with gh 2.101.0 (the version the image pins), an empty `HOME` and no system git configuration: `git fetch` of a private repository this server's gh login reaches, with the environment `forgeEnvironments` gives, exited 128 without `GH_TOKEN` and 0 with it, `FETCH_HEAD` a commit, and nothing git said held the token. The token came from this server's gh login into the process, never printed; the repository is not named here.

**Files outside the issues' own.** `docs/troubleshooting.md` (the known gap of #436 removed, #421's narrowed to the release lock), the matrix and this log.

**Not done here.**
- **No Compose run.** No Docker was used: the fetch in the service's container, and a real restart under Compose, are left to the next rehearsal of the proof (B6.5p).
- **The lock's git.** The v1 release lock (`serve/release-broker.ts`, `merge-pr.ts`, `lib/release.ts`) reads `lib/forge.ts` directly and is unchanged. It fetches and pushes with git itself (`merge-pr.ts`, the base's fetch and the rollback's push in `lib/release.ts`), so in the Compose `broker` container, with no GitHub App, a private repository is still refused there. Changing `lib/forge.ts`'s ambient environment is the v1 decision of point 3; the broker is left for an issue of its own, and `docs/troubleshooting.md` keeps that narrower gap.
- **#425,** GitLab's credential for the flow's git, the sibling of #421, is unchanged.

**Checks**, on this branch at `origin/v2` `0e49cbde`:
- `npm run typecheck` in `v2/`: clean.
- `npm test` in `v2/`: 2878 Node tests, 2743 pass, 135 skipped, 0 fail; 415 Vitest tests pass.
- `test/forge.test.ts` of v1: 15 pass, the ambient credential unchanged.
- `npm run guard -- --base origin/v2`: nothing refused. The guard does not read `docs/v2/`, so the lane's diff was also searched for the owner's name, the organisation's and the first piloted project's: none.

**Resources.** No Docker object, no container, no tunnel, no listening port but the tests' own ephemeral loopback ones. GitHub: the issues, one read-only fetch of a private repository with this server's gh login, and the pull request. No Claude Code login read. Network: `npm ci` of the lock file, `git fetch`.

- Pull request: 454, against `v2`.
- Author: Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), lane `v2-j6-setup-robustness`.

## 2026-10-28: the workspace the assistant writes, used by every module with no restart, and the Tower's tickets named by its id (the author's choices, lane `v2-j6-workspace-reload`, B6.5, M10, P263, issues #420, #437)

**The need.** Milestone 6, issues #420 and #437. The service reloads the workspace without a restart (#420), and the Tower no longer sends an empty project when it creates a ticket after the setup assistant (#437). Acceptance: an end-to-end test runs the assistant, then a first ticket, with no restart, and the ticket carries the right project; a page says which modules follow the workspace with no restart and which need one. Fakes only, nothing on a real server, no deploy. The brief says the milestone 6 plan's section for this lane is quoted in it; it is not, and no milestone 6 plan is in the repository, so the lane follows the two issues, [milestone-5-plan.md](milestone-5-plan.md) for context and the conventions of its section 3.1, as earlier lanes did when `PROMPT.md` was missing.

**The branch.** `v2-j6-workspace-reload`, from `origin/v2` at `0e49cbde` (pull request 448); `origin/v2` merged at `1f49a708` (pull requests 457 and 454), where lane `v2-j6-setup-robustness` had taken P262, so this lane's line is P263.

**What was found.** P256 (#433) had closed the first part of #420: the flow's runtime reads its settings again while it has none and builds the engine at the first request that finds them. Its log entry left three modules that read the workspace at start only: the lead's knowledge, the mirrors and the workspace's record. Reading every module that reads the workspace found more, and a worse case: the knowledge and the notifications were gated on `CLEARED_V2_PROJECT`, and the lead's switch too (`lead/config.ts`), while the assistant writes `CLEARED_V2_WORKSPACE` only (`workspace/connect.ts`). On an install by the assistant these three never started, a restart included.

**Decision.**
1. **One shape for every module: started once the flow runs.** Each module that needs the workspace does what it did at start when the settings name one, else it waits for the flow's engine (`runtime.whenEngine`, P256) and does it then, in the same process. The engine is built from the workspace, so a module that waits for it never reads a half-written file. A module that stops guards its listener with a start count, as the flow module does, so a stop then a start does nothing twice.
   - The tickets module: the workspace's rows (`workspaces`, `services`) and the tracker mirrors.
   - The knowledge module: the lessons proposed from handovers and the daily skill tickets. Its gate is now the workspace the flow reads, not `CLEARED_V2_PROJECT`.
   - The notify module: the dispatcher, started when the settings name a workspace or a project, else once the flow runs.
   - The lead module: the plans, the lead, the quota reading, the service map's first refresh and the schedules' first tick. The lead is on unless `CLEARED_V2_LEAD_ENABLED` turns it off; it still runs only once the flow runs (`lead/engine.ts`), as before.
   - The approver gate (`approval/service.ts`) reads the workspace again while it has none, then keeps it, as the approval key is read (P256, decision 11).
   - Not changed: `cleared run` builds its launcher at the first `POST /api/run`, and the reader of questions to the code at the first question, both on the engine, so both follow it already. The doctor, the test secrets and the environment step read the workspace at each call.
2. **What still needs a restart is written down, not rebuilt.** A workspace changed once the flow runs on one (a repository connected later from the Services screen, or removed) is not taken in place: the engine holds the live sessions, the trains, the timers and the subscriptions on its configuration, and rebuilding it under them is a larger change than the two issues. The environment step already answers `restart` for such a service. `docs/install.md`, new section "What needs a restart", lists it with the heartbeat's quota line (its project is read when the beat starts), the release trains of several repositories, and the service's own settings, with the command (`docker compose -f v2/compose.yaml restart service`). Question 2.
3. **The train approvals are unchanged.** A first try built them once the flow ran too. The end-to-end test, on two repositories, then showed the service refusing them for another reason: the assistant writes no `broker_socket` and no `broker_state`, so both services name the same lock folder ("the services guestbook and filter-api name the same broker state folder: give each its own broker_state: the trains' approvals are refused"). That is decision 21 of milestone 2 (a broker per service), which the Compose file does not run, as P261 says; a restart does not change it. So the change was dropped, and the page says the trains need a lock per repository.
4. **#437: the Tower names the workspace's id.** Option (a) of the issue: the app reads the project from the service's `GET /api/workspace`, which the Tower reads already. A new ticket now names it as a batch did (`ticketProject` in `screens/tower/model.ts`, used by both); the app's project name, the header's label, only when the workspace could not be read. The service still refuses a ticket of another project: option (b) (the service fills a missing project) was not taken, since it would accept a ticket a page sent with no project by mistake.
5. **No string a person reads in the product is added**, so no catalog changes: the changed lines are the service's log (English, for a developer) and the documentation.

**Questions for the owner** (defaults applied):
1. **The lead on an install by the assistant.** It never started there, since its switch read `CLEARED_V2_PROJECT`. (a) On unless `CLEARED_V2_LEAD_ENABLED` turns it off, as for an install by hand (applied): once a repository is connected, a lead session starts and uses Claude Code's quota. (b) Off on an install by the assistant until the owner turns it on in the settings. Recommended: (a), the lead being part of what Cleared is.
2. **A repository connected later.** (a) A restart, said in the environment step and in `docs/install.md` (applied). (b) The flow rebuilt in place once no session runs, a lane of its own. (c) A restart button in the app. Recommended: (a) now, (b) if connecting later turns out to be common.

**Tests first.** `fe0ea4c7` committed the tests alone. On it:
- `test/setup/no-restart.test.ts` failed at the first module that read the workspace at start: "the workspace's rows are written" (`[]`, expected `['guestbook']`). The flow, the workspace step and `GET /api/workspace` already passed, from P256.
- `test/approval/sensitivity.test.ts`, the gate's case, failed with `1 !== 2` (read once, the empty read kept).
- `test/lead/config.test.ts` failed: `loadLeadConfig` said off with a workspace file and no project.
- `app/web/test/tower-workspace.test.tsx`, its new case, failed: `ticketProject is not a function`.
- `test/notify/module.test.ts`, "with a workspace file the dispatcher starts too", was written with the module's change and run on the old module, where it failed.
Changed with the code, each for what the first full run of the end-to-end test showed: its workspace is two repositories and the train approvals' assertion is gone (decision 3); the mirror is seen by its first pass's rows, since that pass asks the tracker nothing; the ticket route answers 200. A last case came from a review of the lane's own diff: `GET /api/lead` builds the lead by itself, so the test now first waits for the lead's session row and the service map's rows, which only the lead module's start makes; with the old `modules/lead.ts` (and the new switch) it failed with "waited 10000 ms for the lead's first generation".

**The end-to-end test** runs main.ts's twelve modules in one process, their settings set before they are imported, as the settings file is applied before anything reads one: a state folder of the temporary folder, no workspace and no project, a fake `gh` over bare copies of the two examples, the fake harness with the proof's first-ticket script (`scripts/proof-j5.ts`), a token file for the GitHub mirror whose address is a recorder on loopback, and a `docker` stand-in first on `PATH`. It makes the owner from the setup code the start printed, as the app does, connects both repositories through the workspace step's routes, then checks that the workspace's rows, the knowledge, the dispatcher, the mirror's two trackers and the lead are there; it creates the first ticket from the first-ticket step and one as the Tower sends it, both with the workspace's id, and waits for the author's session plan in the inbox. The stand-in got no call and the recorder no request.

**CI's first run** (pull request 456, job `verify`) failed in the end-to-end test's cleanup, not in its checks: removing the state folder gave `ENOTEMPTY`, so something was still writing into it during the removal. The Tower-shaped ticket's route starts its author without waiting (`void engine.begin`), and the test ended once the first ticket's plan was in the inbox: read at that moment on this server, the second ticket had no session yet, its checkout and its siblings' exports still under way in git. On the runner, slower (5.4 s against 3 s here), one of those git processes wrote while the folder was removed. It did not happen here in nine runs, under one core and four at once, nor with git slowed down, so the failure was not reproduced as such. The test now waits until both authors' session plans wait in the inbox, which also proves that the Tower's ticket runs in the workspace, and its cleanup closes what the modules' stop leaves to the process's exit (the engine's, the lead's, its plans', its schedules' and the dispatcher's timers), which had printed "lead tick failed" once the ledger was closed. No timeout was changed. CI's second run, on the merge of `origin/v2`, passed that test and failed another, outside this lane: `test/mcp/followups.test.ts`, "the server process whose client closed its stdout exits with 0", with `EPIPE`. The server exits once its stdout closes, as the test wants, and the test's loop can write to its stdin between that exit and the moment `exitCode` says so: the write meets a closed pipe. Reproduced in a script of this server's scratch folder, not in the test itself. The test now ignores an `EPIPE` of its own pipe, and still fails on any other error of it, on an exit code other than 0, or on a word on stderr.

**Files outside the issues' own.** `test/mcp/followups.test.ts` (the race above), `src/setup/steps/environment.ts` and `src/container/types.ts` (comments only, the restart named), `scripts/proof-j5.ts` (one comment: the lead now starts in the rehearsal and plays no act; the rehearsal was not run again), `docs/notifications.md` and `v2/README.md` (the dispatcher's and the flow's start), `docs/install.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` (the known gaps: #437's line removed, #420's replaced by a link to the new section), the matrix and this log.

**Not done here.**
- No Compose run and no rehearsal: the end-to-end test is in one Node process with fakes. `scripts/proof-j5.ts` is unchanged.
- A workspace changed once the flow runs, and the heartbeat's quota line on an install by the assistant: a restart, as written (question 2).
- The release trains of several repositories on a Compose install: a lock per repository (decision 21 of milestone 2), not run by the Compose file.
- No progress dashboard: the owner's rules ask a sub-agent to keep one for a long task, and the brief forbids starting any sub-agent.

**Checks**, on this branch at `origin/v2` `0e49cbde`:

- `npm test` in `v2/`: 2874 Node tests, 2739 pass, 135 skipped, 0 fail; 416 Vitest tests pass.
- `node --test test/setup/no-restart.test.ts`: passes in about 3 s, the stand-in `docker` called by nobody; run again with the lead's case, with `test/docs.test.ts` and `test/scripts/proof-j5.test.ts`: all pass.

- `npm run guard -- --base origin/v2`: nothing refused. The guard does not read `docs/v2/` and ran without the private-term list, so the lane's diff was also searched for the owner's name, the organisation's and the first piloted project's: none.

**Resources.** No Docker object (the test's stand-in refuses every call and got none), no real GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Cursor or Codex account, no Claude Code login read. ## 2026-10-28: a session survives the crash of its container, recreated through the adapter's resume, at most three times (the author's choices, lane `v2-j6-session-survives`, B5.1a, B5.4a, P25, P264, issue #453)

**The need.** Milestone 6, wave 2, issue #453 (linked to #436, done by pull request 454). A session's container that stops before the session is done must be detected by the service, recreated from the same environment on the same checkout, and the session resumed through the adapter's resume; after a fixed number of failures the session stops with a readable reason, with no loop. Acceptance: a test kills a running session's container (`docker kill`, label-filtered, on a container the test made) and the session resumes with no intervention; the thread stays continuous with a "container recreated" event in French and English; the checkout's uncommitted work is kept; the session's cost adds both processes, with no double counting; after three failures the session stops with a visible reason and its Docker objects are cleaned; a session taken over (P25) is never restarted automatically; Claude Code works, and Codex is documented if it cannot resume. Out of scope: a restart of the service itself (#58), moving the agent loop out of the harness, the setup check's resume (#436). The brief names a milestone 6 plan's section for this lane; no milestone 6 plan is in the repository, so the lane follows the issue, the brief and the conventions of [milestone-5-plan.md](milestone-5-plan.md) section 3.1, as lane `v2-j6-workspace-reload` did.

**The branch.** Renamed to `v2-j6-session-survives`, from `origin/v2` at `584d3ebe` (pull request 456).

**What was found.** The pieces were there, not joined. The Claude Code adapter's `stop()` keeps the config volume and its `resume()` starts a new container on the same session (B5.1a; verified with the real harness on 2026-10-21, [adapters.md](../adapters.md)); the checkout is a host bind mount, so it outlives any container; the ticket's cost already read a lower running total as a new process (P211). But a runner that died was `RUN_ERROR` `runner_exit`, which the flow answers by putting the ticket back; and `startSession` refuses a session that still has containers or networks, which a killed session container leaves (its egress, its test services, its siblings, both networks), so a bare `resume()` after a kill fails.

**Decision.**
1. **Where the state lives.** In the flow engine, on the service's side, as for the sessions the idle watchdog stops: the session's id, its `StartInput` (its checkout, model, policy and tools), its phase and its events stay in the engine and the ledger while its container is gone. Nothing moves into the container or out of the harness.
2. **What a lost container is.** The adapter says it: the attached `docker start` ends with no exit line from the runner while no `stop()` runs, which is how a kill, the kernel's out-of-memory killer or the Docker daemon going away end it. That is a new `RUN_ERROR` code, `container_lost` (`CONTAINER_LOST` in `session/contract.ts`), with the exit code in its message. A runner that prints its exit line with a code stays `runner_exit` and is not recreated: it said why, and starting it again would say the same. A removal that `stop()` itself causes is no loss (the new `stopping` flag). The existing adapter test that ended a runner with no exit line now expects `container_lost`, since that is the case it describes.
3. **The recreation.** The engine closes the session at once (so the end of its stream is not read as a failure), keeps it out of the live sessions and in the set the tick never releases, waits, calls the old handle's `stop()` (what the dead container left goes, the volume stays), then the adapter's `resume()` on the same id, journals `cleared.container_recreated` (attempt, limit, how long it waited), supervises the new handle from the last event, and sends the session one message from the flow: its container was recreated on the same checkout, its uncommitted work and its transcript are there, its turn was cut. The thread keeps one numbering: the loss, the recreation, then the session's own words.
4. **The bound.** `CONTAINER_RECREATIONS = 3` recreations per session, whatever ends each attempt; the waits are 5 s, 10 s and 20 s (`RECREATE_BACKOFF_MS`, doubled; `FlowConfig.recreateBackoffMs` for the tests). The loss after the third recreation, or a third attempt whose resume fails, fails the session: `RUN_ERROR` `container_failed` with the reason ("stopped 4 times", or the resume's error), its containers and networks removed by the handle's `stop()`, its config volume removed through the new `forget` dependency (`Docker.removeVolumes`, label-filtered by the session), `session_stopped`, and the ticket back in Todo with the new put-back reason `container_lost`. The count is in memory: a restart of the service is #58's. Question 2.
5. **A session taken over is never recreated** (P25). Its loss stops it with that reason ("the flow never recreates a session taken over"), its ticket back in Todo, as any other failure of a paused session.
6. **A session waiting for a person** (a request in the inbox, or a session plan waiting for its Go) is not recreated at once: it waits as a session the watchdog stopped (`#dormant`), its containers removed, its request still in the inbox. The answer, or the Go, resumes it through the existing `#wake`, which now journals `cleared.container_recreated` for it. So no turn runs and no quota is spent while nobody answered, and an answer is never lost to a container that went away.
7. **While a container is recreated**, a message, a take over or a hand over answers 409 with "being recreated after its container stopped: try again in a moment"; the idle watchdog skips it; a ticket set aside or stopped meanwhile ends the recreation, which then does nothing more. `close()` ends the waits.
8. **The cost needed no change, and a first reading of it was wrong.** The real run of 2026-10-21 ([adapters.md](../adapters.md)) resumed the session in a new container and read 0.00536 USD before and 0.00560 after, where one turn costs about 0.0002 to 0.0006: the resumed Claude Code process goes on with the session's running total, read from its transcript. `sessionsCost` (P211) already takes a session's last total, and adds a total that starts again lower as a new process, so both processes count once. The tests-first commit pinned the opposite reading (the second process from zero, 0.75 expected for 0.30 then 0.45); the first code commit made `sessionsCost` reset at `cleared.container_recreated`, which would have counted the first process twice for the real harness. A review of the lane's diff against that run caught it, and the reset was taken out before the pull request: the tests now pin the last total (0.45), a total that starts again (0.30 then 0.15: 0.45), and the ledger's query, unchanged. The engine's budget stop and a step's cost (`#spent`, `#stepCost`) still sum every turn's running total, as before this lane: they are not the session's cost the acceptance names, and changing the budget's arithmetic is not this issue's.
9. **The thread's words.** The app shows a `RUN_ERROR` by its code when the catalog knows it (`container_lost`, `container_failed`) and the service's English otherwise, and the recreation as its own row ("Container recreated on the same checkout after 5s, attempt 1 of 3: the session carries on, its uncommitted work kept."; in French, "Conteneur recréé sur la même copie de travail après 5 s, tentative 1 sur 3 : la session continue, son travail non commité conservé."). The ticket's note and the session's message are the service's, in English, as every flow note.
10. **`docker kill` in the wrapper.** `Docker.kill(session, name)` kills a session's container by the id a labelled list returned, as `start` and `rm` do; the label gate's test had refused `kill` outright, and now refuses it on any id no labelled list returned and accepts it on an owned one. The acceptance test goes through it; nothing in the service calls it.
11. **Codex and Cursor are not recreated, and it is written down** ([adapters.md](../adapters.md), A session's container that stops; [troubleshooting.md](../troubleshooting.md), the known gaps). Their container's command is `sleep infinity` and each turn is a `docker exec`, so nothing watches the container between turns: a kill shows as that turn's failure and the ticket goes back to Todo, as before. Codex's thread is on the config volume, so a recreated container could resume it; detecting the loss is the missing part.

**Questions for the owner** (defaults applied):
1. **"A readable error in the inbox".** No inbox item kind holds a failed session today: a put back is the ticket's note, the session's failed state and thread, the `ticket_put_back` and `session_stopped` events (the lead and the notifications hear them), and the Tower's ticket back in Todo. (a) As now, with the reason in the session's thread in the person's language and in the ticket's note (applied). (b) A new inbox item for a session that failed for good, with its reason and a link to its thread: an interface lane of its own (the store, the API's types, the inbox screen and its captures). Recommended: (b) if the owner wants to be told in the inbox of every ticket the flow put back, not only this one.
2. **How many failures.** The issue says "beyond 3 failures" and the brief "after 3 failures". (a) Three recreations, the fourth loss stops (applied). (b) Two recreations, the third loss stops. Recommended: (a).

## 2026-10-28: the web app redesigned with Hallmark: Signal, one light theme, every screen recomposed (the author's choices, lane `v2-j6-ui-hallmark`, P265, B3.8, issue #451)

**The need.** The owner asked for a full visual redesign of `v2/app/web` with the Hallmark skill, assertive enough that the difference shows at first glance on every screen, under rules of their own: light only, flat colours checked in CI, no translucent white on information, nothing clickable that moves, no photo and nothing remote, AA contrast, visible focus, 44 px targets, reduced motion, readable figures; logic, routes, forms, texts, test hooks and tests kept, no assertion weakened; the sidebar for the development only.

**The branch.** Renamed to `v2-j6-ui-hallmark`, from `origin/v2` at `1f49a708`; `origin/v2` merged in at `1caf1492` (no conflict).

**Decision.**
1. **A custom theme, Signal.** Hallmark's deal gave Console, Blueprint and Lumen, all on a dark or mid ground, which the light-only rule refuses; the run is custom, from the material of Hallmark's Wayfind (public signage): square 2px ink frames, ink plates carrying one figure, cobalt for the primary action and what is live, amber for what waits. The faces stay Geist and Geist Mono (B3.8), cut heavy for headings and figures, because Wayfind's all-mono face would slow the long French text. The system is locked in `docs/v2/ui-hallmark/DESIGN.md`.
2. **The scale grew, and stays closed.** `tokens.test.ts` held three text sizes and two weights; a heading set large needs more. It now holds six spacing steps, five sizes (13, 14, 20, 28, 40 px) and three weights (400, 600, 800), and every sheet still uses only them. The gradient test lost its one exception (the grace bar's fill had none left).
3. **Dark mode removed.** Its tokens, the sheets' dark blocks, the theme button, the palette's item, the account menu's, the terminal's branch and the catalogs' words are gone; `theme.js` forgets an old choice and always sets light. The browser tests that looped over a dark theme now check that the page stays light under a dark system scheme and an old stored choice (`a11y-browser.test.ts`), that a page told it is dark draws the same paper (`access-browser.test.ts`), that no theme item nor its words exist (`palette.test.ts`) and that the built sheet has no dark rule (`lead/app.test.ts`). The 654 dark captures under `docs/v2/` are removed (the owner's rule); the earlier entries that name them keep their history in git.
4. **The CI check.** `app/test/redesign/flat.test.ts`, Node's modules only, run by the verify job's new step "Flat colours guard" before the install (`runs-on` unchanged): the word gradient in no file of `app/web` or `app/public`, no dark theme, no blurred shadow, no translucent white, no move or scale on a hover or a press, no font or url from another site.
5. **Middle dots and dashes.** Hallmark refuses meta lines joined by two middle dots or more, and dashes in copy. The models' strings are unchanged; `components/facts/Facts.tsx` draws such a line as cells parted by a rule that says a comma to a screen reader, and the tests read it back as the line the model joined. Consumption's period, which Intl writes with an en dash, says "15 au 21 oct. 2026" (new key `consumption_period_to`).
6. **What moved on the page.** No label over a heading: the plan's state follows its title in the document, Consumption's period sits beside its heading. The sidebar is fixed (and the phone's top bar), so only the screen's bar is sticky. A row shows its title and its reason whole rather than cutting them under its meta. The plans screen scrolls as a page. A whole-page capture grows the window to the page's height, so the phone's bar of screens ends the page instead of floating mid-page.
7. **New words**, in both catalogs: `index_groups_label`, `index_group_*` (the sessions grouped as the sidebar groups them) and `consumption_period_to`; removed: `theme_dark`, `theme_light`.

**Sloplint.** Run in a real browser (Chromium through puppeteer-core in a scratch folder) on snapshots of the signed-in screens, their sheets inlined, `--scope app`: tower, sessions, inbox, session, plans, a plan and Consumption at 0 FAIL, two Reflex gates waived in the stamp (64, Geist Mono for ids; 72, the sidebar's session titles cut with an ellipsis). The sign-in page, the service map, a question to the code and the setup steps were not linted again after the last round: listed in the pull request.

**Reviews.** No sub-agent was started (the brief's rule): the hero and finish reviews Hallmark asks for were done in this session, from the captures.

**Resources.** No Docker, no tunnel, no listening port but the tests' and the captures' own ephemeral loopback ones. Network: `npm ci`, `git fetch`, puppeteer-core from npm and oxipng 9.1.5's release archive from its GitHub repository, both into a scratch folder outside the repository; GitHub for the issue and the pull request. ## 2026-10-28: versioned agent profiles, apart from the environment, recorded on each session (the author's choices, lane `v2-j6-agent-profiles`, P266, issue #452)

**The need.** Issue #452: an agent profile (harness, model, role prompts, allowed tools, MCP servers, skills) whose every change is a new version that is never changed, with a rollback; an environment apart (image, network, allowed hosts, CPU and memory), versioned too; each session names the version of each it ran on, in its receipt; `harness: auto` goes through `flow/harness-pick.ts`; a default profile that changes nothing for the sessions that exist; no secret in a profile. Out of scope: sharing profiles between installs, Cursor profiles while P87 stands, a profile changed during a session. The brief names the lane's section of the milestone 6 plan; no milestone 6 plan is in the repository, so the lane follows the issue and the brief, as lanes `v2-j6-workspace-reload` and `v2-j6-setup-robustness` did.

**The branch.** Renamed to `v2-j6-agent-profiles`, from `origin/v2` at `584d3ebe`; `origin/v2` merged at `1caf1492` (pull request 458), where lane `v2-j6-session-survives` had taken P264; then at `c452ab97` (pull request 460), where lane `v2-j6-ui-hallmark` had taken P265, so this lane's line is P266.

**Decision.**
1. **Two objects, each a list of versions in ledger.db.** `agent_profile_versions` and `environment_versions` (`src/profiles/store.ts`), one row per version, its fields as JSON, who wrote it, when, and the version it restores, if any. Triggers refuse any `UPDATE` or `DELETE` of a row, so the ledger keeps the rule, not only the code. An edit names the fields it changes; the rest are the current version's, and the whole is checked again. A rollback writes an old version's fields as the next version, which names it: the versions between stay, and a rollback can be rolled back. An edit or a rollback that would write the current version again is refused (`unchanged`).
2. **Version 1 is the service as it ran, and is read, not written, until the first edit.** Its every field says "the service's": no model (the service's `CLEARED_V2_AUTHOR_MODEL` and `CLEARED_V2_REVIEWER_MODEL` with their rules: the Quick label, the Consumption screen's choice, a service's reviewer sensitivity), no role prompt, no added command, no image (the service's prepared image, else Cleared's), the project's hosts, Cleared's limits. A first try wrote it at every opening of the ledger: `test/store/migrations.test.ts` then failed, since a ledger with no row is no longer one, and the migrations copy it. So an empty table reads as version 1, which is written, with no date, just before version 2. The tables are created by the store itself (`store/db.ts`), after its migrations, so a migration's copy is the ledger as it was; no numbered migration was needed, as nothing that exists changes.
3. **"Exactly as before" is pinned by the inputs `origin/v2` gave.** Before any code, the author's and the reviewer's `StartInput` of a ticket on the fakes were recorded from `origin/v2` at `584d3ebe` (`test/profiles/fixtures/default-inputs.json`); on the default versions the same ticket gives the same inputs, and no image or limits key. The image matters most: naming one skips the service's prepared image (C15), so the default names none.
4. **What a profile and an environment apply, and how.**
   - The author's and the reviewer's models: the profile's one comes after the Consumption screen's choice, which stays the owner's switch of the moment, and before the service's; the rule that the reviewer is another model holds for it. Question 2.
   - A prompt per role, added after the first prompt of each author or reviewer session, 4,000 characters at most.
   - The allowed commands: added to the policy's safe commands after Cleared's and the project's, which only an author's policy reads (a reviewer runs its own reads). Each names its command first, so a bare `*` that would allow every command is refused. The policy matches the safe commands after its deny rules (a push to the base, a forced push) but before its asks (`simple` in `session/policy.ts`): a deletion past the ticket's files, `curl` to an undeclared host, an install. Any signed-in person can write a profile, while a project's own `[session] safe_commands` goes through its review; so the allowed commands are an allowlist, word by word (`tool` in `profiles/store.ts`, after the review of pull request 459, below): the program is a literal name and none that runs another command, a shell, the network, an install or a deletion (`rm`, `curl`, `ssh`, `npx`, `sudo`, `env`, `xargs`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `busybox`, the shells, the package managers that are runtimes too, and a few more); `git`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` and `pip` name one of their safe subcommands literally (reads, the tests, `run`, `add` and `commit` for git), never `push`, `install`, `exec` or `reset`; an interpreter runs a script named literally, or a test or check module after `python -m`, never `-e`, `-c` or pip; and the policy's `*` comes only where the policy reads every option it can stand for: after a program of the policy's `READ_OPTIONS` (`cat`, `head`, `tail`, `ls`, `wc`, `grep`, `rg`; exported as `OPTION_READ_PROGRAMS`), or after `git status`, `diff`, `log`, `add` or `commit`, which Cleared's own safe commands already allow with one and whose options the policy checks. A test runner's or a linter's options load code (`--config`, `--require`, `--plugin`) and the policy does not read them, so those are allowed exactly as written. Any other command is allowed exactly as written, as an "Always in this project" answer allows one. What is refused stays a question.
   - The network: `project` (the model API, the npm registry, the project's hosts and the environment's) or `model-only` (the first two). Both go through the session's egress proxy; neither opens more than that list.
   - The image: one Cleared builds, `cleared-v2-<name>:<tag>`, given to Claude Code's sessions only, since Codex's and Cursor's images carry their own program. The CPUs (0.5 to 16) and the memory (256m to 64g) go to every harness's container, over Cleared's limits (`limitsOf`, `container/session-runtime.ts`).
   - MCP servers and skills: a session has no MCP server beyond Cleared's own and mounts the project's skills as they are (B5.5b), and nothing in the runtime takes another value yet. The fields are in each version, saying so, and any other value is refused (`mcp`, `skills`) rather than kept and ignored, which would make a version claim what a session did not get. Question 4.
5. **Harness: `claude-code` or `auto`, P87 untouched.** The three `HARNESS = 'claude-code'` of the engines are unchanged and `test/session/cursor/reachability.test.ts` passes as it was. Codex and Cursor are no profile's own harness; they are reached through `auto`, which makes a new ticket a harness pick (P213, the same code path as `harnesses` on `POST /api/tickets`) on the harnesses `CLEARED_V2_PICK_HARNESSES` enables whose adapter is registered, when there are two at least, on a workspace of one service. With the default gate (Claude Code alone) a ticket runs as before, on Claude Code. A ticket that names its number of variants or its harnesses keeps them: what the person asked for that ticket comes first. A Quick ticket keeps its fast lane on Haiku (decision 15 of milestone 2), and a setup session (C4) its one author: neither becomes a pick. Each session records `auto` with its versions, and its harness is the one the pick ran it on (the `sessions` row's own column). `test/flow/harness-pick.test.ts` is unchanged and passes. Question 3.
6. **Each session's versions.** `session_profiles`, one row per author or reviewer session, written when it starts and never changed (a trigger again). The versions are read once at the start of `#launch`, before any wait, in the same turn as the model the caller read, so the model and the version recorded are one. An author or a reviewer session from before profiles has no row and reads as run on version 1 of each, which is what it ran on; the lead and a reader have no profile and show none. A handover starts a new session, on the versions current then. The session screen's ticket card says the versions (and, on `auto`, the harness the pick chose); the pull request's receipt says the versions its sessions ran on, "1, then 2" when an edit fell during the ticket.
7. **No secret.** Every text of a change, each key with its value as a line would write it, is read against the guard's patterns (`GUARD_PATTERNS`, `session/clean.ts`) and the token shapes it leaves to the private-term list (GitHub, GitLab, Slack, a cloud key, a bearer token, an assignment mid-sentence, credentials before a host). A match is refused with the field's path and the pattern's category, never the value; the API answers `{ "error": "sensitive" }` (a catalog key with "secret" in its name reads as an assigned secret to the guard). The harness's login stays mounted from the service (B5.4e).
8. **The routes and the screen.** `GET /api/profiles`, `POST /api/profiles/agent`, `/agent/restore`, `/environment`, `/environment/restore`, served by the flow module (no thirteenth module) behind the app's proof and a person the service knows, with or without an engine. The Services screen gets one panel under the test secrets, with the tokens and the button of the test secrets' panel: both histories, newest first, the current version marked, Restore on the others. Changing a field is done through the API. Question 1. The lane `v2-j6-ui-hallmark` redesigns the screens in parallel, so the panel adds no new token or component.

**Questions for the owner** (defaults applied):
1. **Editing in the app.** (a) The API for changes, Restore in the app (applied). (b) A form per field on the Services screen, once the redesign lands. Recommended: (b) after `v2-j6-ui-hallmark`.
2. **Which model wins.** (a) The Consumption screen's choice, then the profile's, then the service's (applied). (b) The profile's first. Recommended: (a); the switch is meant for the moment.
3. **`auto` and the quota.** With two harnesses or more enabled, every new ticket runs as a pick, several authors at once. (a) As said, behind `CLEARED_V2_PICK_HARNESSES`, which stays unset until the owner's trials (applied). (b) `auto` for the tickets of some types only. Recommended: (a) until the trials say what a pick costs.
4. **MCP servers and skills.** (a) Refused beyond today's value until a lane gives sessions a way to take them (applied). (b) Kept in the version and not applied. Recommended: (a).
5. **`npm test *` in Cleared's defaults.** It takes npm's options, so `npm test --script-shell=<file>` runs that file without a question, profile or not. (a) Left as it is here, named by a test (applied). (b) A lane narrows the default to `npm test` and `npm test -- *`. Recommended: (b), as an issue of its own.

**Tests first.** `0611e97e` committed the tests and the recorded inputs alone. On it the new files did not load (`src/profiles/store.ts` and `src/profiles/routes.ts` missing), and the adapter's case failed with `actual: [ '--memory', '4g', ... ]`, `expected: [ '--memory', '2g', ... ]`. Changed with the code, each for what the code showed: the triggers' case saves an environment version too, since an empty table now holds no row to refuse a change of; the opening case says a ledger opened is not written; the receipt's line reads "Agent profile version: 1", since its catalog test refuses a French sentence equal to the English one; the panel's case reads the agent's history alone. `test/flow/modules.test.ts` names the five new routes, and `app/web/test/i18n-audit.test.tsx` lists "Version {version}" and "Claude Code" among the words French writes as English does.

**The review of pull request 459** (head `c92e6b6`, one blocker). The first rule was a denylist of command heads, `^git\s+(?:push|...)`, and the policy's `*` matches inside a word as well as whole words: `git *` passed it, and with it the policy allowed `git push origin feat`; `npm *` allowed `npm install left-pad` and `npm exec foo`. The rule is now the allowlist of decision 4. `test/profiles/policy.test.ts` puts every pattern of a list (wildcards anywhere, the wrappers, inline code) through `readProfile`, gives the policy those it accepts, and checks that none of 37 commands (a push, a reset, an install through npm, pnpm, yarn, pip or `python -m pip`, `npx`, `curl` alone or behind `timeout`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `busybox`, `env`, a shell, `rm`, `awk` with `system`, `tar --to-command`) is allowed, while `npm run lint --fix`, `git log`, `make check`, a script and `python -m pytest` still are; a second case shows the same commands allowed by the policy under `git *`, `npm *` and `timeout *`, so the first case tests what it says. Both files failed on the commit reviewed (`git *` accepted) and pass now. The review's two nits are fixed too: the matrix line's closing bar, and a sentence said twice under "Not done here". CI's `verify` then failed `test/flow/never-deploys.test.ts` on that head: the list of programs a profile refuses named a cluster tool the test keeps out of the service's code. It is gone from the list and nothing is weaker: with the allowlist, a program outside the read and check tools takes no wildcard, so that tool and the other deploy tools the test names are refused with one (`test/profiles/store.test.ts` checks four, their names built from parts), and an exact command is a person's deliberate choice, as an "Always in this project" answer is. The full `npm test` passed then: 2933 Node tests, 2789 pass, 144 skipped (the browser tests), 0 fail; 423 Vitest tests. One run before it failed `test/flow/one-service.test.ts` once, outside this lane: a session's random UUID held a digit run the cleaner's phone pattern removes, so its message id was not the one the test normalizes; it passed alone three times and in the next full run. `origin/v2` merged again at `c452ab97` (pull request 460, the redesign of lane `v2-j6-ui-hallmark`, which took P265): the panel takes the redesign's tokens with no change of its own, and its captures in `docs/v2/agent-profiles/` were taken again.

## 2026-10-28: learning from past sessions, a nightly pass per service that proposes in the inbox what reviewers asked for on two tickets or more (the author's choices, lane `v2-j6-dreaming`, P267, issue #455)

**The need.** Issue #455: a periodic pass per repository over the sessions' transcripts and the reviewers' refusals, which proposes a rule or a change of skill in the inbox, each proposal citing its source sessions; nothing applied without the owner's Approve; two source sessions at least; the proposals through the secret filter, tested with a token planted in a transcript; a rejected proposal never proposed again; the pass off per repository and within the quota threshold; no duplicate of what the memory holds (#217, point 3). Out of scope: automatic application, learning across repositories or installs, any model training, any Linear work. The brief names the lane's section of the milestone 6 plan; no milestone 6 plan is in the repository, so the lane follows the issue and the brief, as the other lanes of the wave did.

**The branch.** Renamed to `v2-j6-dreaming`, from `origin/v2` at `c40a7e91` (pull request 459, which took P266), so this lane's line is P267. Lane `v2-j6-ui-pro` claims P266 on its own branch too; the merge order decides who renumbers.

**Decision.**
1. **The proposal is the handovers' knowledge item.** A pass's proposal is a `knowledge` item at the service's level, so it goes through the circuit that exists (C2, P27, O12): Approve, the owner's only, writes it into the memory and queues it for the service's skill, whose daily Quick ticket lands through the lock; Reject writes nothing. The pass itself writes only the inbox item and its own record. Its ticket is `dreaming` (`DREAM_TICKET`), which no tracker has, its id `knowledge:dream:<service>:<n>`, its `sessionId` the newest source, and a new field `sources` lists one `{ session, ticket, at }` per ticket, newest first. Approve writes it as a lesson (`Lesson: ...`), as a handover's lesson is. Question 1.
2. **What is read.** The reviewers' change requests on the review channel (`cleared.review_channel` from the reviewer), on reviewer sessions only: the flow journals each request on the author's session too, which would count one refusal twice. Thirty days back, the newest first, at most 500. A request's defects are the lines of its Defects section, as the review prompt asks for them (`defectsOf`), without the leading `file:line`; "None." is none.
3. **What is a group.** Two defects are one rule when 60 % of their words are shared (`knowledge/fingerprint.ts`: lower case, no accents, no punctuation or markdown, no `file:line`, no number, no small English or French word). A group cites one source per ticket, the newest reviewer session of each, and needs two tickets: a reviewer resumed over its rounds is one session, and two reviewers of one ticket are one ticket, since a defect asked for again on the same ticket is a defect not yet fixed, not a recurring one. The proposal's text is the newest wording, in the reviewer's language. At most five per service and night, the groups seen on the most tickets first.
4. **No secret.** A defect is left out of every group when it matches the guard's patterns (`GUARD_PATTERNS`) or the forges' and clouds' token shapes the profiles refuse (`TOKEN_PATTERNS`, now exported from `profiles/store.ts`), when it holds a `[removed` mark of the cleaner, or when the service's cleaner would change it; the chosen text is read again before it is stored. The review channel's text is cleaned when it is journaled, but the guard's list leaves a GitHub or cloud token to the private-term check, so the second list matters: without it the test fails.
5. **Never proposed again.** `Knowledge.reject` keeps the rejected item's words in `knowledge_rejected`, for every knowledge item, a handover's included, so the rule holds even if the inbox lost the item. A group is not proposed when any of its defects shares the words of a rejected rule, of an approved entry (`knowledge_skill`, what the inbox wrote into the memory) or of any knowledge item, waiting or answered.
6. **When, and the switch.** From 02:00 of the server's day, the hour before the skill tickets, once per service and day, checked every ten minutes as the skill tickets are; a restart the same day does nothing more. Each service is on until the owner turns it off (`dreaming_settings`, `POST /api/dreaming/:service`, the owner only, as Approve; the Services screen's panel). At the week stop (`CLEARED_V2_WEEK_STOP_PERCENT`, 85 % by default, read by `quotaStop` as the plans and the batches read it) the pass is skipped, recorded as `quota`, and tried again at the next tick.
7. **No model.** The pass reads and compares words: it spends no quota and calls nothing, in the tests or in production. Question 2.

**Questions for the owner** (defaults applied):
1. **Where an approved proposal lands.** (a) The memory and the service's skill, through the knowledge circuit and the lock (applied). (b) A new version of the agent profile (P266), the rule added to the author's role prompt. Recommended: (a); the issue puts the profile's prompts out of scope, and (b) would wait for a form to edit a profile.
2. **A model to write the rule.** (a) None: the newest wording of the defect (applied). (b) A read-only session per group, like the reader's, that writes the rule from the defects, under the week stop and counted in Consumption. Recommended: (a) until the owner has seen a few weeks of proposals.
3. **On by default.** (a) On for every service (applied: the issue says nightly by default, and it costs nothing). (b) Off until the owner turns it on.
4. **The cost in Consumption.** The pass costs nothing, so Consumption has nothing to add; the issue's box "the cost of the pass appears in Consumption" stays unticked. (a) As is (applied). (b) A line on the Consumption screen saying the pass is free. Recommended: (a); (b) comes with question 2 (b).

**Tests first.** `e5e3e55e` committed `test/knowledge/dreaming.test.ts` alone; on it the file did not load (`src/knowledge/dreaming.ts` missing). Then each rule was checked by breaking it: without `TOKEN_PATTERNS` the secret case fails; without the rejection's record the "never again" case fails; with one source per session instead of per ticket the "fewer than two" case fails; without the quota check the week stop case fails; with every service on the switch's case fails. The inbox's case was written after its code and fails on the card without it. The panel's browser case (`app/test/services/dreaming-browser.test.ts`) found a fault of the first panel: each box was disabled while its change was sent, so it lost the keyboard's focus and a second Space did nothing; a box now stays enabled and a change sent while another is on its way is ignored, the section saying it is busy.

**Files outside the issue's own.** `src/profiles/store.ts` (`TOKEN_PATTERNS` exported), `src/api/types.ts` (the routes, `KnowledgeSource`, `DreamingView`), `src/inbox/store.ts` (`addDreamed`), `test/api/types.test.ts` (the two routes), `app/fixtures/` (a proposal of the pass, the pass on the fixtures' services), `.github/workflows/v2.yml` (the new browser test in the browser job's list; `runs-on` unchanged), the matrix and this log. The panel's captures are in `docs/v2/dreaming/` (1440, 768 and 390 pixels, and in French at 1440).

**Not done here.**
- Only the reviewers' requests are read: not a person's permission refusals, nor a person's edits of an author's files. A ticket put back after too many rounds leaves its last report on the ticket, not on the channel, so that report is not read.
- What the memory holds from outside the inbox (an older `lib/memory` entry) is not compared: the comparison is with what the inbox wrote (`knowledge_skill`) and every knowledge item.
- No capture of the inbox's card: the fixtures' inbox is shared by the other browser tests, so the pass's proposal is not added to it; the card is proven by `app/web/test/inbox/additions.test.tsx`, in both languages.
- No progress dashboard: the owner's rules ask a sub-agent to keep one for a long task, and the brief forbids starting any sub-agent.
